questions.question: If f(x) = [a|x|+x²-2(sin|x|)(cos|x|)]/x for x≠0, and f(x)=b for x=0, is continuous at x=0, then a+b is equal to:
questions.solution: Using left/right limits with expansion: -a+2 = a-2 = b gives 2a=4, so a=2, b=0, and a+b=2.

questions.question: Let π/2<θ<π and cotθ = -1/(2√2). Then the value of sin(15θ/2)(cos8θ+sin8θ) + cos(15θ/2)(cos8θ-sin8θ) is equal to:
questions.solution: Expression simplifies to cos(θ/2)-sin(θ/2) = -√(1-sinθ). Using cotθ=-1/(2√2), sinθ=2√2/3, giving -√((3-2√2)/3) = (1-√2)/√3.

questions.question: Let a = î-2ĵ+3k̂, b = 2î+ĵ-k̂, c = λî+ĵ+k̂ and v = a×b. If v·c=11 and the length of the projection of b on c is p, then 9p² is equal to:
questions.solution: Solving determinant equation gives λ=1. Projection of b on c = b·ĉ = 2/√3 = p. So 9p² = 9(4/3) = 12.

questions.question: Let A(1,2) and C(-3,-6) be two diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus, whose sides AD and BC are parallel to the line 7x-y=14. If B(α,β) and D(γ,δ) are the other two vertices, then |α+β+γ+δ| is equal to:
questions.solution: Midpoint of A and C is (-1,-2), so (α+γ)/2=-1 and (β+δ)/2=-2, giving |α+β+γ+δ|=|-2-4|=6.

questions.question: Consider two sets A = {x∈Z : ||x-3|-3|≤1} and B = {x∈R-{1,2} : [(x-2)(x-4)/(x-1)]log_e(|x-2|)=0}. Then the number of onto functions f:A→B is equal to:
questions.solution: A={-1,0,1,5,6,7} (6 elements), B={3,4} (2 elements). Number of onto functions from a 6-element set to a 2-element set = 2⁶-2 = 62.

questions.question: The system of linear equations x+y+z=6; 2x+5y+az=36; x+2y+3z=b has:
options: unique solution for a=8 and b=16
infinitely many solutions for a=8 and b=14
infinitely many solutions for a=8 and b=16
unique solution for a=8 and b=14
questions.answer: infinitely many solutions for a=8 and b=14
questions.solution: D=0 when a=8. For a=8, D1, D2, D3 are all zero only when b=14, giving infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: The sum of all the real solutions of the equation log_(x+3)(6x²+28x+30) = 5 - 2log_(6x+10)(x²+6x+9) is equal to:
questions.solution: Substituting A=log_(x+3)(6x+10) gives A+4/A=4 or A=2, solving to x²=1, x=±1. Sum of roots = 0.

questions.question: If the points of intersection of the ellipses x²+2y²-6x-12y+23=0 and 4x²+2y²-20x-12y+35=0 lie on a circle of radius r and centre (a,b), then the value of ab+18r² is
questions.solution: Using family of curves S1+λS2=0 with λ=1/2 gives the circle x²+y²-16x/3-6y+27/2=0, centre (8/3,3), radius r=√(47/18). ab+18r²=8+47=55.

questions.question: Let PQ be a chord of the hyperbola x²/4 - y²/b² = 1, perpendicular to the x-axis such that OPQ is an equilateral triangle, O being the centre of the hyperbola. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is √3, then the area of the triangle OPQ is:
questions.solution: e=√3 gives b²=8, hyperbola x²/4-y²/8=1. Solving with 30° angle condition gives sinθ=1/√6, and area = 4√2·sinθ/cos²θ = 8√3/5.

questions.question: Let a, b, c be three vectors such that a×b = 2(a×c). If |a|=1, |b|=4, |c|=2, and the angle between b and c is 60°, then |a·c| is:
questions.solution: b-2c=λa with λ²=16 gives λ=±4. Dotting b-2c=±4a with c gives |a·c|=1.

questions.question: Bag A contains 9 white and 8 black balls, while bag B contains 6 white and 4 black balls. One ball is randomly picked from bag B and mixed with bag A. Then a ball is randomly drawn from bag A. If the probability that the ball drawn is white is p/q, gcd(p,q)=1, then p+q is equal to:
The area of the region enclosed between the circles x²+y²=4 and x²+(y-2)²=4 is:
questions.solution: Integrating the intersection area: A = 4∫₀^√3(√(4-x²)-1)dx = 8π/3 - 2√3 sq. units, which equals (2/3)(4π-3√3).

questions.question: The least value of (cos²θ - 6sinθcosθ + 3sin²θ + 2) is
questions.solution: Simplifying gives f(θ) = 4 - 3sin2θ - cos2θ, which ranges in [4-√10, 4+√10]. Least value is 4-√10.

questions.question: Let I(x) = ∫3dx/[(4x+6)√(4x²+8x+3)] and I(0) = √3/4 + 20. If I(1/2) = a√2/b + c, where a,b,c∈N, gcd(a,b)=1, then a+b+c is equal to:
questions.solution: Substitution 4x+6=1/t leads to I(x) = (3/4)√[(4x+2)/(4x+6)] + c, with c=20. Evaluating at x=1/2 gives I(1/2) = 3√2/8 + 20, so a=3,b=8,c=20, sum=31.

questions.question: The number of ways, in which 16 oranges can be distributed to four children such that each child gets at least one orange, is
questions.solution: Using stars and bars with each ≥1: reduces to x1'+x2'+x3'+x4'=12, giving C(15,3)=455 solutions.

questions.question: Let A={0,1,2,...,9}. Let R be a relation on A defined by (x,y)∈R iff |x-y| is a multiple of 3. Statement I: n(R)=36. Statement II: R is an equivalence relation.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: n(R) = 4×4+3×3+3×3 = 34 (not 36), so Statement I is false. R is reflexive, symmetric, transitive, so it is an equivalence relation — Statement II is true.

questions.question: If z = √3/2 + i/2, i=√-1, then (z²⁰¹-i)⁸ is equal to
questions.solution: z=cos(π/6)+isin(π/6). z²⁰¹ = cos(201π/6)+isin(201π/6) = -i. (z²⁰¹-i)⁸ = (-2i)⁸ = 256.

questions.question: If the mean and the variance of the data (Classes 4-8,8-12,12-16,16-20 with frequencies 3,λ,4,7) are μ and 19 respectively, then the value of λ+μ is
questions.solution: μ = 10+60/(λ+14), requiring λ+14 to divide 60 evenly. Using variance condition gives 19λ²-28λ-516=0, so λ=6, μ=13, λ+μ=19.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle OAB is inscribed in the parabola y²=4x with vertex O at the vertex of the parabola. Then the minimum distance of the circle having AB as a diameter from the origin is
questions.solution: Using slope=tan30° gives t=2√3. Circle centre at (12,0), radius 4√3. Least distance = 12-4√3 = 4(3-√3).

questions.question: Let Σ_{k=1}^n a_k = αn²+βn. If a10=59 and a6=7a1, then α+β is equal to
questions.solution: a10 gives 19α+β=59; a6=7a1 gives 11α+β=7(α+β), leading to 2α=3β. Solving: α=3, β=2, α+β=5.

questions.question: If the solution curve y=f(x) of the differential equation (x²-4)y' - 2xy + 2x(4-x²)² = 0, x>2, passes through the point (3,15), then the local maximum value of f is
questions.solution: d(y/(x²-4)) = -2x dx integrates to y=(-x²+C)(x²-4). With (3,15): C=12. y'=0 at x=2√2, giving local maximum y = ((2√2)²-4)(-(2√2)²+12) = 16.

questions.question: If the image of the point P(a,2,a) in the line x/2=(y+a)/1=z/1 is Q and the image of Q in the line (x-2b)/2=(y-a)/1=(z+2b)/-5 is P, then a+b is equal to.
questions.solution: Setting up the reflection equations for both lines and solving simultaneously gives b=2a and a=1, so b=2, a+b=3.

questions.question: The number of elements in the set S={x : x∈[0,100] and ∫₀ˣ t²sin(x-t)dt = x²} is.....
questions.solution: Integration by parts reduces the integral equation to x²-2(1-cosx)=x², giving cosx=1, so x=0,2π,4π,...,30π — 16 total elements.

questions.question: Let A = [[0,2,-3],[-2,0,1],[3,-1,0]] and B be a matrix such that B(I-A) = I+A. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of B^T B is equal to
questions.solution: Since A^T=-A, computing B^T B = (I+A)^{-1}(I+A)(I-A)(I-A)^{-1} = I. Trace of B^T B = trace(I) = 3 (3x3 identity).

questions.question: Let S denote the set of 4-digit numbers abcd such that a>b>c>d and P denote the set of 5-digit numbers having product of its digits equal to 20. Then n(S)+n(P) is equal to.
questions.solution: n(S)=C(10,4)=210 (choosing 4 distinct digits and arranging in decreasing order). For n(P): digit combinations (5,4,1,1,1) and (5,2,2,1,1) give 5!/3!+5!/(2!2!) = 20+30 = 50. Total = 210+50 = 260.

questions.question: The internal energy of a monoatomic gas is 3nRT. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of 17 cm² fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by supplying 126 J heat. If the temperature rises by 4°C, then the piston will move ____ cm. (atmospheric pressure = 10⁵ Pa)

A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio 2:2:3. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of 18 m/s each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is ____ m/s.
questions.solution: Conservation of momentum: 2(-18î)+2(-18ĵ)+3V3=0, giving V3=12î+12ĵ, |V3|=12√2 m/s.

questions.question: A block is sliding down on an inclined plane of slope θ and at t=0 is given an upward momentum so it starts moving up with velocity u. The distance S travelled by the block before its velocity becomes zero is ____.
questions.answer: Dropped by JEE (correct result u²/(2gsinθ) does not match any option)
questions.solution: Using v²=u²-2gsinθ·s: s = u²/(2gsinθ) — this doesn't match any of the given options (which use cosθ instead of sinθ), so JEE dropped the question.

questions.question: The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of an equilateral triangle of side 4√3 cm is 2A. The magnetic field at its centroid is α×10⁻⁵ T. The value of α is ____. (μ0=4π×10⁻⁷ SI units)

A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after 2s of free fall and starts decelerating with 3 m/s². At 10 m height from ground, descending with the parachute, the speed is 5 m/s. The initial height of the aeroplane is ____ m. (g=10 m/s²)
questions.solution: Free fall for 2s: x1=20m, v=20m/s. Deceleration phase: 5²=20²-2(3)x2, x2=62.5m. Final phase: x3=10m. Total H=20+62.5+10=92.5m.

questions.question: Two short dipoles (A,B), A having charges ±2μC and length 1cm and B having charges ±4μC and length 1cm are placed with centres 80cm apart. The electric field at point P, equidistant from centres of both dipoles is ____ N/C.
questions.solution: P1=2×10⁻⁸, P2=4×10⁻⁸ Cm. Net field combining perpendicular components (axial and equatorial) gives |E_net| = (9×10⁴/16)√2.

questions.question: Two charges 7μC and -2μC are placed at (-9,0,0)cm and (9,0,0)cm respectively in an external field E=A/r² r̂, where A=9×10⁵ N/C·m². Considering the potential at infinity is 0, the electrostatic energy of the configuration is ____ J.
questions.solution: V=A/r for the external field. U = U_self + U_interaction = q1V1+q2V2+kq1q2/(2r) = 50-0.7 = 49.3 J.

questions.question: A bead P sliding on a frictionless semi-circular string (ACB) is at point S at t=0 with horizontal velocity component v. Another bead Q ejected from A at t=0 along horizontal string AB with speed v. Let tp and tQ be respective times taken to reach point B. The relation between tp and tQ is
questions.solution: Horizontal displacement of Q is greater than P (XQ>XP), and since horizontal velocity component is the same for both, tQ=XQ/v > tp=XP/v.

questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2mm and maintaining connections, it draws 25% more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is ____.
questions.solution: Combining series-parallel capacitance model: Ceq = Kε0A/(2+3K). Setting 1.25×(ε0A/5) = Ceq gives 0.25(2+3K)=K, so 2+3K=4K, K=2.

questions.question: To compare EMF of two cells using a potentiometer, the balancing lengths obtained are 200 cm and 150 cm. The least count of scale is 1 cm. The percentage error in the ratio of EMFs is ____
questions.answer: Dropped by JEE (calculated value ≈1.16% doesn't match any option)
questions.solution: Δy/y = Δℓ1/ℓ1 + Δℓ2/ℓ2 = 1/200+1/150 = 7/600 ≈1.16%, which doesn't match any given option, so the question was dropped.

questions.question: An air bubble of volume 2.9 cm³ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool 5m deep. At the bottom, water temperature is 17°C. The volume of the bubble at the surface, where temperature is 27°C, is ____ cm³. (g=10 m/s², density of water=10³ kg/m³, 1 atm=10⁵ Pa)
questions.solution: Using P1V1/T1=P2V2/T2 with P1=Patm+ρgh: V2 = 4.5 cm³.

questions.question: Which of the following pair of nuclei are isobars of the element?
questions.solution: Isobars are nuclei with the same mass number; ³H and ³He both have mass number 3.

questions.question: For a given logic gate circuit (OR gate feeding a NAND gate with one input direct and other from OR output), which is the correct truth table for inputs n,m and output z?
questions.solution: Output z = NOT(n·(n+m)) = NOT(n) = n̄. Truth table: (n,m,z) = (0,0,1),(0,1,1),(1,1,0),(1,0,0), matching option 4.

questions.question: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas expands from volume V to 2V isothermally at 27°C and does W joule of work. If the gas undergoes the same magnitude of expansion adiabatically from 27°C doing the same amount of work W, then its final temperature will be (close to) ____ °C.
questions.solution: W_isothermal = RT ln2 = 300R(0.693). Setting W_adiabatic = nR(T1-T2)/(γ-1) equal to this and solving gives T_final ≈ 216.84 K ≈ -56.3°C.

questions.question: A prism of angle 75° and refractive index √3 is coated with a thin film of refractive index 1.5 only at the back exit surface. To have total internal reflection at the back exit surface, the incident angle must be ____. (sin15°=0.25, sin25°=0.43)
questions.answer: Answer options given as [1,2,4] meaning i < 25° satisfies multiple listed ranges (i≈25°, so i<25° or i≤20°); precise computed value i=25°
questions.solution: For TIR at back surface, r2≥60°, so r1≤15°, giving sin i = √3 sin15° = 0.433, i≈25°. This satisfies i<25° (and consequently the 'between 15° and 20°' and '<15°' ranges are approximately consistent per JEE's multiple accepted answers 1,2,4).

questions.question: A circular loop of radius 7cm is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.2T perpendicular to its plane. The loop is converted into a square loop in 0.5s. The EMF induced in the loop is ____ mV.
questions.solution: Circumference=14π cm, side of square = 14π/4 = 7π/2. Δφ=B(A1-A2)=6.614×10⁻⁴ Wb. EMF=Δφ/0.5=1.32×10⁻³ V=1.32mV.

questions.question: A long solenoid of 100cm length, radius 2cm, 500 turns per unit length, carries current I=10sin(ωt)A, ω=1000rad/s. A circular loop (B) of radius 1cm coaxially slides through the solenoid at speed v=1cm/s. The rms current through loop B when inserted 10cm inside is α/√2 μA. The value of α is ____. (Resistance of loop=10Ω)
questions.solution: Induced current i = πr²μ0ni0ω/(√2 R) ≈ 197/√2 μA, so α=197.

questions.question: The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant k=3 and permeability μ=2μ0, is (μ0=permeability of vacuum)
questions.solution: C/V = √(εrμr) = √(3×2) = √6, giving ratio √6:1.

questions.question: When unpolarized light falls at a particular angle on a glass plate (in air), the reflected beam is linearly polarized. The angle of refracted beam with respect to normal is ____. (tan⁻¹(1.52)=57.7°, refractive indices of air and glass are 1.00 and 1.52 respectively)
questions.solution: At Brewster's angle, tan i = μg/μa = 1.52, so i=57.7°. Refraction angle r=90°-i=32.3°.

questions.question: A small metallic sphere of diameter 2mm and density 10.5 g/cm³ is dropped in glycerine having viscosity 10 Poise and density 1.5 g/cm³. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is ____ cm/s. (π=22/7, g=10 m/s²)

numerical_questions.question: The average energy released per fission for the nucleus of ²³⁵U is 190 MeV. When all the atoms of 47g pure ²³⁵U undergo fission, the energy released is α×10²³ MeV. The value of α is ____. (Avogadro Number=6×10²³/mole)
numerical_questions.solution: Moles of U-235 = 47/235 = 1/5 mol. Total energy = (1/5)×6×10²³×190 = 228×10²³ MeV, so α=228.

numerical_questions.question: The size of images of an object formed by a thin lens are equal when the object is placed at two different positions 8cm and 24cm from the lens. The focal length of the lens is ____ cm.
numerical_questions.solution: Using m1=-m2 with m=f/(f+u): f/(f-8) = -f/(f-24), giving f-8=24-f, 2f=32, f=16 cm.

numerical_questions.question: A ball of radius r and density ρ dropped through a viscous liquid of density σ and viscosity η attains its terminal velocity at time t, given by t=Aρ^a r^b η^c σ^d, where A is a constant and a,b,c,d are integers. The value of (b+c)/(a+d) is ____.
numerical_questions.solution: Dimensional analysis gives c=-1, a+c+d=0, -3a-c-3d+b=0, leading to b=2, a+d=1, so (b+c)/(a+d) = 1/1 = 1.

numerical_questions.question: A uniform circular disc of mass M kg and radius r m has shaded regions cut out (as shown). The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis A is X/256 Mr². The value of X is ____.
numerical_questions.solution: Using parallel axis theorem for the cut-out smaller discs (radius r/4) and subtracting from the full disc's moment of inertia, the result simplifies to I = 109MR²/256, giving X=109.

numerical_questions.question: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from 0°C to α°C. The value of α is ____.

questions.question: A concentration vs time plot for a dissociation reaction A→nB is given. Based on the data of the initial phase of the reaction (initial 10 min), the value of n is ____.
questions.solution: At t=0, [A]=0.05; at t=10min, [A]=0.04, [B]=0.01×n. Change in A (0.01) relates to B formed (0.03), so 0.01n=0.03, n=3.

questions.question: It is noticed that Pb²⁺ is more stable than Pb⁴⁺ but Sn²⁺ is less stable than Sn⁴⁺. Reactions: PbO2+Pb→2PbO (ΔrG°(1)); SnO2+Sn→2SnO (ΔrG°(2)). Identify the correct set.
questions.solution: Since Pb²⁺ is more stable, reaction 1 is spontaneous (ΔrG°(1)<0). Since Sn²⁺ is less stable, reaction 2 is non-spontaneous (ΔrG°(2)>0).

questions.question: In an electrochemical cell with a metal electrode M undergoing M→M⁺+e, the cation M⁺ is present at two concentrations c1 and c2 separated by a semi-permeable membrane. Which statement is correct for generating a positive cell potential?
options: If c1 is at anode, then c1=c2
If c1 is at cathode, then c1<c2
If c1 is at cathode, then c1>c2
If c1 is at anode, then c1>c2
questions.answer: If c1 is at cathode, then c1>c2
questions.solution: For a concentration cell, positive E_cell requires the cathode to have higher concentration than the anode. If c1 is at cathode, E_cell = -0.059log(c2/c1) > 0 requires c2<c1, i.e., c1>c2.

questions.question: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of
questions.solution: DNA and RNA are chiral due to the chiral 2-deoxy-D-ribose and D-ribose sugar units respectively.

questions.question: Identify the CORRECT set of details: A. [Co(NH3)6]³⁺: Inner orbital complex, d²sp³. B. [MnCl6]³⁻: Outer orbital complex, sp³d². C. [CoF6]³⁻: Outer orbital, d²sp³. D. [FeF6]³⁻: Outer orbital, sp³d². E. [Ni(CN)4]²⁻: Inner orbital, sp³.
questions.solution: Co³⁺ with NH3 (SFL): d²sp³, inner orbital (A correct). Mn³⁺ with Cl⁻ (WFL): sp³d², outer orbital (B correct). Co³⁺ with F⁻ (WFL): sp³d² not d²sp³ (C incorrect as stated). Fe³⁺ with F⁻ (WFL): sp³d², outer orbital (D correct). Ni²⁺ with CN⁻ (SFL): dsp², inner orbital, not sp³ (E incorrect).

questions.question: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of X and phosphorus is higher than that between phosphorus and Y. X & Y are respectively
questions.solution: EN values: N=3.0, P=2.1, As=2.0. |EN(N)-EN(P)|=0.9 > |EN(P)-EN(As)|=0.1, so X=N, Y=As.

questions.question: Statement I: (CH3)3C⁺ is more stable than •CH3⁺ as nine hyperconjugation interactions are possible in (CH3)3C⁺. Statement II: •CH3⁺ is less stable than (CH3)3C⁺ as only three hyperconjugation interactions are possible in •CH3⁺.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution: Statement I is correct due to nine hyperconjugative C-H bonds available. Statement II is false since methyl cation CH3⁺ has no alkyl hydrogens for hyperconjugation (it's a primary carbocation with no adjacent C-H for hyperconjugation in the way described).

questions.question: Iodoform test can differentiate between: A. Methanol and Ethanol. B. CH3COOH and CH3CH2COOH. C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone. D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one. E. Anisole and acetone.
questions.solution: Ethanol gives positive iodoform test (methanol doesn't) - A correct. Acetone gives positive iodoform test (anisole doesn't) - E correct. Acetic acid, cyclohexanone, and pentan-3-one do not give the iodoform test as they lack the CH3-CO- or CH3-CH(OH)- group.

questions.question: Statement I: The second ionisation enthalpy of Na is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of Mg. Statement II: The ionic radius of O²⁻ is larger than that of F⁻.
options: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Statement I is true but statement II is false
questions.answer: Both statement I and statement II are true
questions.solution: Na⁺ has a stable fully-filled noble gas configuration, so removing a second electron requires much more energy than for Mg⁺ (which still has one electron to lose from a stable config easily) - Statement I true. O²⁻ has a larger ionic radius than F⁻ due to greater electron-electron repulsion for the same number of protons - Statement II true.

questions.question: A dibromocyclopentane derivative undergoes (i) Zn, Δ (ii) HBr to give major product P. Identify (P).
questions.solution: Zn/Δ causes debromination to form a cyclopentene ring fused system; addition of HBr proceeds via the more stable carbocation with a 1,2-hydride shift, giving the rearranged bromide product (structure 2).

questions.question: Reactions at T(K): I. A→products. II. 5Br⁻(aq)+BrO3⁻(aq)+6H⁺(aq)→3Br2(aq)+3H2O(l). Both reactions started at 10:00am; rates are equal at 10:10am. -Δ[Br⁻]/Δt at 10:10am is 2×10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹min⁻¹. Concentration of A at 10:10am is 10⁻² mol L⁻¹. What is the first order rate constant (min⁻¹) of reaction I?
questions.solution: Rate of reaction II = (1/5)(2×10⁻⁴) = 4×10⁻⁵ mol/L/min. Setting this equal to k[A]: 4×10⁻⁵=k×10⁻², k=4×10⁻³ min⁻¹.

questions.question: Which statements are TRUE about the Haloform reaction? A. NaOCl reacts with KI to give KOI. B. KOI is a reducing agent. C. α,β-unsaturated methylketone (CH3-CH=CH-CO-CH3) will give iodoform reaction. D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test. E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.
questions.solution: NaOCl+KI→NaCl+KOI (A correct). KOI is an oxidizing agent, not reducing (B incorrect). The α,β-unsaturated methyl ketone still contains the CH3-CO- group and gives iodoform reaction (C correct). Isopropyl alcohol does give a positive iodoform test (D incorrect). Methanoic (formic) acid does not give iodoform test (E incorrect).

questions.question: Which statements are NOT TRUE about XeO2F2? A. It has a see-saw shape. B. Xe has 5 electron pairs in its valence shell. C. The O-Xe-O bond angle is close to 180°. D. The F-Xe-F bond angle is close to 180°. E. Xe has 16 valence electrons in XeO2F2.
questions.solution: The molecule does have a see-saw shape (A true). Xe actually has 7 electron pairs, not 5 (B false/not true). O-Xe-O bond angle is close to 120°, not 180° (C false/not true). F-Xe-F bond angle is close to 180° (D true). Xe has 14 valence electrons in this molecule, not 16 (E false/not true). So B, C, E are the NOT TRUE statements.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statements: A. Notation ²⁴₁₂Mg represents 24 protons and 12 neutrons. B. Wavelength of radiation of frequency 4.5×10¹⁵ s⁻¹ is 6.7×10⁻⁸ m. C. One radiation has λ1=900nm, energy=E1; another has λ2=300nm, energy=E2, E1:E2=3:1. D. Number of photons of light of wavelength 2000pm that provides 1J of energy is 1.006×10¹⁶.
questions.solution: ²⁴₁₂Mg has 12 protons and 12 neutrons, not 24 protons (A incorrect). λ=c/v=6.67×10⁻⁸m (B correct). E1/E2=λ2/λ1=300/900=1/3, not 3:1 (C incorrect). Number of photons = Energy/(hc/λ) = 10¹⁶ (D correct, close to stated value).

A mixed ether (P), when heated with excess hot concentrated HI produces two different alkyl iodides which when treated with aq. NaOH give compounds (Q) and (R). Both (Q) and (R) give yellow precipitate with NaOI. Identify the mixed ether (P):
questions.solution: Ether cleavage with excess conc. HI gives ethyl iodide and sec-butyl iodide; hydrolysis gives ethanol (Q) and sec-butanol (R), both of which contain the CH3-CH(OH)- pattern and give positive iodoform/NaOI test.

questions.question: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed in the reaction between KI and acidified K2Cr2O7 solution is:
questions.solution: K2Cr2O7 + KI + H⁺ → I2 + Cr³⁺; chromium is reduced from +6 to +3 in the final product.

questions.question: The work functions of two metals (MA and MB) are in 1:2 ratio. When exposed to photons of energy 6eV, the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of MA:MB is in ratio 2.642:1. The work functions (in eV) of MA and MB are respectively.

Statement I: 3,4-diaminotoluene-type diamine can be synthesized from the corresponding diethyl-substituted arene using i) acidic KMnO4, ii) ammonia, iii) bromine and alkali. Statement II: p-toluidine can be converted into 3,5-dibromotoluene using reagents (i) Br2-H2O, (ii) NaNO2/HCl (0-5°C), (iii) aq. H3PO2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution: Statement I: KMnO4/H+ oxidizes side chains to carboxylic acids, converted to amide via NH3, then Hofmann bromamide (Br2+KOH) gives the diamine — correct sequence. Statement II: Bromination directs ortho to NH2, diazotization then H3PO2 replaces the original amino group with H, leaving the dibromo product — correct sequence.

questions.question: A student is given compound 'x' of molecular formula C6H7N. 'x' is sparingly soluble in water but becomes soluble with dilute mineral acid. 'x' with CHCl3 and KOH(alc.) gives 'y' with unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, 'x' gives compound 'z' soluble in alkali. The number of different H atoms present in 'z' is:
questions.solution: x is aniline (C6H5NH2). Carbylamine reaction with CHCl3/KOH gives phenyl isocyanide (y, unpleasant smell). Hinsberg test with benzenesulphonyl chloride gives N-phenylbenzenesulfonamide (z, soluble in alkali since it's a secondary sulfonamide from a primary amine). Counting distinct H environments in Ph-NH-SO2-Ph gives 7 different types of H atoms.

numerical_questions.question: X2(g) + Y2(g) ⇌ 2Z(g). X2(g) and Y2(g) are added to a 1L flask and the system attains equilibrium at T(K) with moles of X2(g), Y2(g), and Z(g) being 3, 3 and 9 mol respectively. Under this equilibrium condition, 10 mol of Z(g) is added and temperature maintained at T(K). Then the number of moles of Z(g) in the flask at the new equilibrium is ____. (Nearest integer)
numerical_questions.solution: Kc=(9)²/(3×3)=9. Adding 10 mol Z shifts reaction backward: (19-2X)²/((3+X)(3+X))=9, giving (19-2X)/(3+X)=3, X=2. New moles of Z=19-2(2)=15.

numerical_questions.question: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At 320K, the vapour pressure of the solution containing 3 mol A and 1 mol B is 500 mmHg. At the same temperature, if 1 mol of A is further added, vapour pressure increases by 20 mmHg. Vapour pressure (in mmHg) of B in the pure state is ____. (Nearest integer)
numerical_questions.solution: 3P°A+P°B=2000 (from first condition); 4P°A+P°B=2600 (from second, with total 4 mol A, 1 mol B, Ps=520). Subtracting: P°A=600 mmHg, P°B=200 mmHg.

numerical_questions.question: 200 cc of x×10⁻³M potassium dichromate is required to oxidise 750 cc of 0.6M Mohr's salt solution in acidic medium. Here x =
numerical_questions.solution: Using n-factor equivalence: equivalents of K2Cr2O7 = equivalents of Mohr's salt (Fe²⁺). (200×x×10⁻³×6)/1000 = (750×0.6×1)/1000, solving gives x=375.

numerical_questions.question: Total number of unpaired electrons present in the central metal atoms/ions of [Ni(CO)4], [NiCl4]²⁻, [PtCl2(NH3)2], [Ni(CN)4]²⁻ and [Pt(CN)4]²⁻ is ____.
numerical_questions.solution: Ni(CO)4: Ni⁰, sp³, 0 unpaired. [NiCl4]²⁻: Ni²⁺, sp³ (tetrahedral, WFL), 2 unpaired. [PtCl2(NH3)2]: Pt²⁺, dsp², 0 unpaired. [Ni(CN)4]²⁻: Ni²⁺, dsp² (SFL), 0 unpaired. [Pt(CN)4]²⁻: Pt²⁺, dsp², 0 unpaired. Total unpaired = 2.

numerical_questions.question: Benzene + CH3-CO-CH2-CH2-CO-Cl reacts via anhydrous AlCl3 to give (P), then aq. NaOH/Δ gives (Q). In compound (Q), the percentage of oxygen is ____ %. (Nearest integer)
numerical_questions.solution: Friedel-Crafts acylation gives keto-acid chloride product P (aryl ketone with pendant CH3-CO- group); intramolecular aldol condensation with aq. NaOH/Δ gives a cyclic enone (Q) with molecular mass 158. %O = (16×2/158)×100 ≈ 10.12% ≈ 10%.
